text: As a child, Theo was fascinated by the stars and spent countless nights stargazing from the rooftop of his rural home. This love for astronomy was more than just a hobby; it was a bond with his late mother, an astrophysicist who nurtured his curiosity about the universe. She used to tell him that the fluffy things in the sky, the clouds, were the ones that rain came from, teaching him that even the most transient and soft-looking phenomena had powerful, life-giving purposes. This lesson grounded his cosmic wonder in earthly reality, driving him to pursue a career where he could bridge the gap between the vastness of space and the tangible needs of people on the ground.
